chapter_name: Framing the Constitution: The Beginning of a New Era
learning_objective: 📜 Step into the Constituent Assembly to witness the intense debates, the struggle for rights, and the drafting of the rulebook for the world's largest democracy!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: संविधान सभा (The body of elected representatives who drafted the Constitution)
उद्देश्य प्रस्ताव (Nehru's resolution outlining the ideals of the Constitution)
पृथक निर्वाचिका (Voting system where only members of a specific community vote for their candidate)
संघीय व्यवस्था (Division of power between the Central government and State governments)
अस्पृश्यता (The oppressive social practice abolished by Article 17)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The Constituent Assembly did its work against the backdrop of the bloody Partition of India. The trauma of riots and mass migration heavily influenced the framers, convincing them to create a very strong Central government to prevent further division.

Introduced by Jawaharlal Nehru on Dec 13, 1946, it declared India as an 'Independent Sovereign Republic'. It guaranteed justice, equality, and freedom to all citizens, and promised adequate safeguards for minorities and depressed classes.

B. Pocker Bahadur argued strongly for separate electorates for Muslims. However, leaders like Sardar Patel and G.B. Pant fiercely opposed it, arguing that this British policy of 'divide and rule' had already caused the tragic partition of the country.

The Assembly formally abolished 'untouchability'. Recognizing historical injustices, the Constitution provided for reservations (reserved seats) in the legislature and government jobs for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to ensure their political voice.

A bitter debate arose over the national language. R.V. Dhulekar pushed for Hindi, while Southern members like G. Durgabai strongly resisted it. A compromise was reached: Hindi in Devanagari script would be the 'Official Language', but English would continue to be used for 15 years.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Balancing Act of Power
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are drafting the rules for a new country. Should the Central Government have all the power, or should the States? Because of the fear of the country breaking apart after Partition, B.R. Ambedkar and Nehru ensured that the Center was given far more sweeping powers than the States!

exam_tips: 📌 The provisions of the 'Objective Resolution' are a highly repeated board question. Memorize its key points.
📌 Be ready to explain *why* 'Separate Electorates' were considered a 'poison' by nationalist leaders like Sardar Patel.
📌 Remember the key figures: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Chairman of the Drafting Committee), Dr. Rajendra Prasad (President of the Assembly), and B.N. Rau (Constitutional Advisor).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949, and fully came into effect on January 26, 1950.
⭐ The Assembly had nearly 300 members and it took almost 3 years (165 days of meetings) to complete the drafting.
⭐ Mahatma Gandhi believed that 'Hindustani' (a blend of Hindi and Urdu) should be the national language because it was easily understood by common people.
